```{r}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse) # for {dplyr} functions
library(rio) # for importing data
library(here) # for easy file referencing
library(sf) # for shapefiles
library(lubridate) # to work with dates
library(survival)
```

# Raw Data
import data:
```{r}
## enrollment data (everyone)
# rn1 <- here::here("data", "RN1.csv") %>%
#   rio::import() %>% 
#   dplyr::as_tibble()
rn2 <- here::here("data", "RN2.csv") %>% # assign participant ID
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()
so1 <- here::here("data", "SO1.csv") %>% # house demographics, etc
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

## clinical data (everyone)
arms <- here::here("data", "arms-blocks.csv") %>% # trial arm
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()
# suspected <- here::here("data", "VA5.csv") %>% # suspected cases
#   rio::import() %>% 
#   dplyr::as_tibble()
actsurv <- here::here("data", "VAR6.csv") %>% # active surveillance results
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

## serology subset
sero <- here::here("data", "Serology Survey.csv") %>% # serology test results
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()
```

merge prep:
```{r}
## merge....prep?
### give participants a unique ID
rn2p <- rn2 %>% 
  # remove REDCap stuff
  select(-c(redcap_event_name, redcap_repeat_instrument,
            redcap_repeat_instance)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(rn2_pt_id) & rn2_cnst_n2 == 1) %>% 
  mutate(ID = paste0(record_id, LETTERS[rn2_pt_id])) %>% 
  relocate(ID)
armsp <- arms %>% 
  select(-c(redcap_event_name, redcap_repeat_instrument,
            redcap_repeat_instance)) %>% 
  mutate(ID = paste0(record_id, LETTERS[a_pt_id])) %>% 
  relocate(ID)

### ok these also depend on year
# susp <- suspected %>% # do i need this? active surv results (below) i think
#   # summarizes all the test results from suspected cases
#   select(-c(redcap_event_name, redcap_repeat_instrument,

#   relocate(Year, .after = record_id)
actsp <- actsurv %>% 
  select(-c(redcap_event_name, redcap_repeat_instrument,
            redcap_repeat_instance, var6_no)) %>% 
  mutate(ID = paste0(record_id, LETTERS[var6_pt_id])) %>% 
  relocate(ID) %>% 
  mutate(Year = year(mdy(var6_rpt_date))) %>% 
  relocate(Year, .after = record_id) %>% 
  # ok var6_abv_pos is total, should i also make a variable that's by season???
  mutate(Pos_2021 = ifelse((Year == 2021 & var6_abv_pos___1 == 1), 1, 0),
         Pos_2022 = ifelse((Year == 2022 & var6_abv_pos___1 == 1), 1, 0),
         Pos_2023 = ifelse((Year == 2023 & var6_abv_pos___1 == 1), 1, 0)) %>% 
  relocate(c(var6_abv_pos___1, Pos_2021, Pos_2022, Pos_2023), .after = Year)

### by house, not by participant
### so just get rid of redcap names
so1p <- so1 %>% 
  select(-c(redcap_event_name, redcap_repeat_instrument, 
            redcap_repeat_instance))

## subset of main population, also for different endpoint (infection) ?

            redcap_repeat_instance)) %>%

  relocate(ID)
```

merge together:
```{r}
## big merge???
full <- actsp %>% # year + id + house
  full_join(rn2p, by = c("ID", "record_id")) %>% # id + house
  full_join(armsp, by = c("ID", "record_id")) %>% 
  full_join(so1p, by = c("record_id")) %>% # house
  arrange(ID) %>% 
  relocate(c(var6_abv_pos___1, a_block), .before = var6_pt_id)
```

Fine, what if I just assume rn2 has a list of all participants for now and they
all lasted until the end of the three year follow up period
```{r}
# cleaning ? organizing merged dataset
full_org <- full %>% 
  mutate(Pos_All = ifelse(is.na(var6_abv_pos___1), 0, var6_abv_pos___1)) %>% 
  relocate(Pos_All, .before = Pos_2021)
  # each individual has an ID, house id, and year/season?

# subset data by season??
yr_one <- full_org %>% 
  filter(is.na(Year) | Year == 2021) %>% 
  mutate(Positive = ifelse(is.na(Pos_2021), 0, Pos_2021)) %>% 
  mutate(Entry = mdy("7/1/2021"),
         Exit = ifelse(Positive == 0, "12/31/2021", 
                       var6_symp_date),
         Exit = mdy(Exit)) %>% 
  relocate(c(Entry, Exit, Positive), .before = Year)

# anyone there twice?
yr_one %>% group_by(ID) %>% summarize(n = n()) %>% arrange(desc(n))
yr_one %>% filter(ID == "123838B" | ID == "387712C")
# both reported and tested twice but both times were negative
# only count them once ?
yr_one_unique <- yr_one %>% 
  group_by(ID) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup()

# km.......?
km_yr_one <- survfit(Surv(as.numeric(Entry), as.numeric(Exit), 
             Positive) ~ 1, data = yr_one_unique)
plot(km_yr_one) # lol
```
